title: the Sepik Basin Rising
premise: Lena Amberdale, a riverboat captain hiding from a past conviction she never deserved, ferries cargo along the Sepik Basin's treacherous waterways. When a dying prospector named Elias Voss trades her a map to an unclaimed gold seam in exchange for a promise—deliver it to his daughter in the highlands—Lena inherits both a fortune and a target. A corrupt mining syndicate, led by the magistrate who framed her, wants the map and will burn the river country to get it. With monsoon season closing in, a leaking hull, and an unexpected ally in a disgraced surveyor named Tomas Reyes, Lena must navigate flooded gorges, betrayals, and her own buried identity to reach the seam first. In the end, she chooses justice over gold: exposing the magistrate's crimes at the basin's great confluence gathering, claiming her name back, and finding that the promise she kept was the treasure all along.
about_author: Coral Sterling is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons working the waterways of Papua New Guinea before turning to fiction. Their adventure novels are known for vivid river landscapes and protagonists who find redemption far from any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Establishes her solitary life piloting the riverboat Kestrel through the Sepik Basin, dodging sandbars and officials alike. She pays off a debt to a harbor boss while avoiding questions about her real name. Emotional beat: weary self-containment, the comfort of invisibility about to crack.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Weight
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She pulls a feverish, half-drowned prospector, Elias Voss, from the reeds. He clutches a oilskin-wrapped map and begs passage upstream. Lena refuses—until he offers payment enough to clear her debt. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion wrestling with hard-learned caution.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, fading in and out of delirium. He reveals the map leads to an unclaimed gold seam and asks Lena to swear she'll deliver it to his daughter, Mara, in the highlands settlement of Karawari Bend. He dies at dawn. Emotional beat: grief and the weight of a dying man's trust settling on unwilling shoulders.

chapters.title: Men in Clean Boots
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Syndicate agents arrive at the dock asking after Voss, led by the smooth-talking Mr. Calloway. Lena lies, but recognizes their warrant's signature: Magistrate Hessler—the man who convicted her on false testimony years ago. Emotional beat: old fear igniting into something hotter.

chapters.title: Leaking Toward the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She slips the Kestrel out at night with a patched hull and dwindling supplies. The boat takes on water faster than expected; she barely beaches it at a trading post. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve—she can't turn back now.

chapters.title: The Surveyor Who Drowned His Maps
chapters.summary: Tomas Reyes's POV. Introduced at the trading post: a disgraced government surveyor drinking away his career after refusing to falsify land claims for the syndicate. He recognizes the map's terrain instantly. Lena hires him as navigator. Emotional beat: two exiles recognizing each other.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: Alternating Lena/Tomas POV. They run the Bakari rapids together; Tomas proves his worth reading water, Lena proves hers reading people when they spot syndicate scouts ahead and bluff past a checkpoint. Emotional beat: fragile partnership forged under pressure.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. At a village stop, elders tell stories of the gold seam being sacred ground, and of Hessler's men burning a village years ago to hide a massacre. Tomas realizes the map is also evidence. Emotional beat: dawning moral stakes beyond personal survival.

chapters.title: Calloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Calloway corners her at a mission station, offering full pardon and a new name if she hands over the map—and reveals he knows exactly who 'Lena Amberdale' used to be. Emotional beat: temptation and fury intertwined; her cover is gone.

chapters.title: Monsoon Breaks
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The rains hit early and violent. The Kestrel nearly founders in a flash flood; they lose half their cargo and shelter in a limestone cave where Tomas finds fresh syndicate survey markers—Hessler's men are already mapping the route. Emotional beat: nature and enemies closing in together.

chapters.title: The Stowaway
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They discover a teenage boy, Iri, hidden among the crates—a village orphan fleeing syndicate recruiters. Lena wants to leave him at the next village; Iri knows a shortcut gorge no outsider does. Emotional beat: grudging acceptance; the crew becoming something like family.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Fuel Depot
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A supposed ally from Tomas's old agency sells their position to Calloway. Syndicate men board the Kestrel at night; Lena fights them off but takes a knife wound, and the fuel stores are sabotaged. Emotional beat: paranoia and the cost of trusting anyone.

chapters.title: Fever Country
chapters.summary: Iri's POV. With Lena delirious from the infected wound, Iri and Tomas navigate by her earlier instructions, poling through flooded forest. Iri sees Lena's vulnerability and tells Tomas fragments of her past she'd never share. Emotional beat: tenderness discovered in caretaking.

chapters.title: The Medicine Woman of Ambunti
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A river healer saves Lena's arm and, in exchange for the story of her conviction, gives her proof: names of witnesses Hessler silenced, which the healer's brother smuggled out years ago. Emotional beat: healing the body and reclaiming the truth in parallel.

chapters.title: Karawari Bend
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They reach the highlands settlement and find Mara Voss—not the grateful heir expected, but a hardened woman running a waystation for laborers escaping the syndicate mines. Mara doesn't trust the map's delivery. Emotional beat: the promise complicated by the daughter's own wounds.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Mapmaker
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara explains her father mapped the seam to prove the syndicate was poisoning the watershed, not to claim gold. The map's coordinates match the massacre site. She agrees to go—but only to expose Hessler, not enrich anyone. Emotional beat: purpose aligning; the quest transforms.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Echoes
chapters.summary: Full crew POV rotation. Iri guides them through the shortcut gorge as the monsoon peaks. Calloway's gunboat traps them mid-passage; Tomas sacrifices the Kestrel, scuttling her to block the channel, and they escape overland with the map and evidence. Emotional beat: devastating loss transformed into liberation from the boat that was her hiding place.

chapters.title: What Lena Buried
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On the mountain trail, Lena finally tells the whole story: she was a clerk who found Hessler's ledger of bribed verdicts and was framed for theft to silence her. Tomas and Mara convince her she isn't running from guilt—she's carrying evidence. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into testimony.

chapters.title: The Seam
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They reach the site: not glittering wealth but a poisoned, scarred valley where syndicate test-mining already killed the river's fish. They photograph everything, copy the map, and cache the originals. Emotional beat: horror and clarity—the gold was never the point.

chapters.title: The Confluence Gathering
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Dozens of river communities gather annually at the great confluence for trade and dispute-settlement outside colonial courts. The crew plans to present the evidence there, where no magistrate holds sway. Calloway's men infiltrate the crowd. Emotional beat: taut anticipation; justice assembling itself.

chapters.title: Judgment at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. Before the assembled villages, Lena testifies under her true name; Mara presents the map and massacre evidence; silenced witnesses step forward emboldened. Calloway tries to seize the documents and is subdued by the very boatmen he's exploited. The gathering strips Hessler's authority and declares his warrants void. Emotional beat: cathartic reckoning—justice rendered by the community the law abandoned.

chapters.title: Downstream, Under Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, epilogue. Monsoon ends. With Hessler fled and the syndicate under investigation, the crew refloats a salvaged hull and signs a contract ferrying witnesses and supplies for the valley's restoration. Lena registers the new boat under her real name. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—an identity reclaimed, a river finally home.
